headline: The Champion Drafted Three Quarterbacks
lede: Two hundred and twenty-four picks, $2,790 spent, seventy-two players gone for a dollar. Three rosters cannot legally fill a lineup. The most expensive player in league history now belongs to a team that has never made the playoffs. And the two men who joined this league eight months ago just out-drafted almost everybody who has been here for a decade. Grades below. Bring a lawyer.

rankings.blurb: Bijan, A.J. Brown, and the two best discounts of the night. The rookie built the cleanest roster in the league and he did it on his first try.
The most core capital in the draft and a five-times-market edge at tight end. Also a one-dollar quarterback and eight one-dollar everything-elses.
Four real starters, only two dollar players, and Mahomes plus Herbert for a combined ten dollars. The other new guy also gets it.
A hundred and eleven dollars on Nacua and Achane, then he kept buying. Highest ceiling outside the top three, thinnest margin for a hamstring.
Seven starters between $17 and $35 and not one player who can end his season alone. He paid three of the five biggest raises to get there.
Chase and McCaffrey is the best pair anybody owns. Seventy-two percent of the budget says everything after them is somebody else's problem.
Barkley, Jeanty and Nico all came in under last year's price. Then a rookie at $13 was asked to be the third receiver.
Paid the two biggest raises of the draft, sixty percent of his budget, for Smith-Njigba and Cook. Parker Washington cost more than three Kelces.
Jonathan Taylor plus three real receivers is a playoff spine. Rico Dowdle at $13 is the second running back, which is the whole problem.
One hundred and thirty-one dollars on wide receivers, thirty-four on the entire backfield. The lineup starts two backs and two flexes.
Josh Jacobs at $8 was the buy of the night and it does not matter, because there is no kicker and no defense on the roster.
Record $73 for Gibbs, $29 for a quarterback, and then nine players at a dollar or two. Six seasons, zero playoff appearances, one very expensive running back.
One hundred and ninety-five dollars spread perfectly evenly across sixteen forgettable players, with no kicker, no IDP and five dollars never spent.
The champion benched $48, bought three quarterbacks for one slot and two kickers for another, and drafted no defensive player at all.

awards.label: The Steal
awards.note: Josh Jacobs at $8. This exact room paid $43 for him last September. He came off the board fifth and fourteen people watched it happen.

awards.label: The Record
awards.note: $73 for Jahmyr Gibbs, the most expensive player in fifteen years of this league. The old record was $70 and that team finished sixth.

awards.label: Most Money Benched
awards.note: $48 of $200 is behind the starting eleven, three and a half times the league average of $14. The defending champion has the smallest active roster in the league.

awards.label: The Empty Chairs
awards.note: Two rosters with no kicker. One of them also has no defense, the other has no IDP. Three mandatory slots, zero players, thirty-two roster spots used.

awards.label: Best Shape
awards.note: $194 of $200 in the starting eleven, seven players over $10, and only six dollar bills. The best-constructed roster belongs to a man in his first draft.

awards.label: The Bravest Twenty-One Dollars
awards.note: Parker Washington cost $21. Travis Kelce cost $6. DK Metcalf cost $19. No notes.

awards.label: Quietest Correct Answer
awards.note: Patrick Mahomes at $3 and Justin Herbert at $7 in a four-point-passing-touchdown league, while the rest of the room spent $153 on quarterbacks.

Fwamming Gwaggon.headline: The new guy read the room
body: Second name called all night, $69 for Bijan Robinson, and then he never panicked again. A.J. Brown at $45, David Montgomery at $23, Jaylen Warren at $13. Seven players over $10 on a roster with only six dollar bills in it. That is not a rookie draft. That is somebody who watched the first four nominations, worked out what this room overpays for, and then bought the parts nobody was looking at.

The back half is where it was won. Brian Thomas Jr. cost $10. This exact room paid $50 for him last September. Courtland Sutton cost $5 after going for $27 a year ago. Two of the four biggest discounts of the night, both his, both while everybody else was still arguing about running backs. $194 of his $200 is in the starting eleven, second most in the league.

The only wobble is Colston Loveland at $22, which is a $3 tight end from last year in a market that averaged $7.80 tonight. Pay that price and you need him to be the position. If he is not, this is a very good team with an expensive hole at the least important spot on the roster. Everything else about this draft was a warning shot at twelve men who have been here for years.
Fwamming Gwaggon.best: Brian Thomas Jr., $10. The same fourteen people paid $50 for him twelve months ago.
Fwamming Gwaggon.worst: Colston Loveland, $22. Almost three times what the tight end market cleared at.

A dad.headline: Four players, eight dollar bills, one prayer
body: $189 of core capital, the most in the league, and $170 of it is in four men: Amon-Ra St. Brown at $60, Kenneth Walker III at $43, Brock Bowers at $39 and Ladd McConkey at $28. Then it stops. Chuba Hubbard at $10 is the RB2. Brian Robinson at $3 is the RB3. Eight players cost a dollar. There is no middle class on this roster at all.

The Bowers buy is the smartest thing anybody did tonight and the easiest to sneer at. Tight end cleared at $7.80 across twenty-four players. He paid $39, which sounds insane until you remember he now has a five-times-market edge at a mandatory slot every single week while thirteen other people start a coin flip there.

Then he spent $1 on Kyler Murray to be his quarterback and $1 on a kicker, which is either a man who has read the scoring settings very carefully or a man who ran out of money and hoped. Given the top-heavy build, both answers are true at the same time. If St. Brown or Walker misses a month, this roster has nothing behind them but ones.
A dad.best: Brock Bowers, $39. The tight end market cleared at $7.80 and he bought a weekly advantage.
A dad.worst: Kenneth Walker III, $43. Eighteen dollars more than this room paid last year for the same player.

The Asshouse Always Wins.headline: Nobody told the rookie to panic
body: Derrick Henry $45, Drake London $45, Chris Olave $32, Breece Hall $29. Four real starters, none of them a budget-ending purchase, and then the most disciplined back half in the draft: only two dollar players on the entire roster. Every other team has at least four. He bought sixteen players and fourteen of them cost real money.

The quarterback room is the joke of the night at somebody else's expense. Justin Herbert cost $7. Patrick Mahomes cost $3. Ten dollars for both, in a room where one man spent $29 on a single quarterback and another spent $22 on three of them. In a league that pays four points for a passing touchdown, that is the correct answer and he is the only person who wrote it down.

The bill comes due on Chris Olave at $32, an $8 player in this room last year, and on a bench that cost $16. Neither is fatal. Two new managers joined this league in the offseason and both of them just out-drafted most of the people who have been here for a decade.
The Asshouse Always Wins.best: Patrick Mahomes and Justin Herbert for $10 combined, in a four-point-passing-touchdown league.
The Asshouse Always Wins.worst: Chris Olave, $32. He was an $8 player in this room in September.

Poop Squad 💩.headline: A hundred and eleven dollars of hamstring
body: Puka Nacua at $63 and De'Von Achane at $48 is $111, fifty-six percent of the budget, on two players whose entire fantasy value is a function of staying upright. When they play they are top-five at their position. The plan is not complicated and it does not need to be.

What saves the grade is that he kept buying afterward. Davante Adams $24, Rhamondre Stevenson $19, MarShawn Lloyd $17, Sam LaPorta at $7 after going for $15 last year. That is a real bench and a real flex. Coming off 7-21 and thirteenth, this is a roster with an actual ceiling rather than another year of watching.

The quarterback plan is Jaxson Dart at $7 with Baker Mayfield at $1 behind him, which is fine right up until it is the only thing anybody talks about. And $17 for MarShawn Lloyd is paying a starter's price for a player who has never held the job. Aggressive is the right posture from where he finished. This is aggressive.
Poop Squad 💩.best: Sam LaPorta, $7. Eight dollars cheaper than last year for the same tight end.
Poop Squad 💩.worst: MarShawn Lloyd, $17. That is real money for a hypothesis.

Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.headline: Seven guys who might all be good
body: The flattest competitive roster in the draft. Rashee Rice $35, Javonte Williams $33, Trey McBride $30, Travis Etienne $28, Tetairoa McMillan $22, Cam Skattebo $21, Rome Odunze $17. Seven starters between $17 and $35, top three share of only forty-nine percent, and no single player who can end the season by pulling up on a Sunday. Coming off the Sacco, that is exactly the correct rebuild.

The problem is what he paid to get there. Rashee Rice went from $6 to $35. Javonte Williams went from $8 to $33. Travis Etienne went from $9 to $28. He personally paid three of the five biggest raises in the entire draft, which means he is not buying value, he is buying last year's breakouts at this year's ceiling. That works if they repeat. Nobody in this league has ever repeated anything except Andrew.

Travis Hunter at $1 after costing $16 a year ago is the kind of pickup that quietly wins a flex spot in October. The floor here is much higher than last season's disaster. The ceiling is capped by the fact that he bought seven number twos and no number one.
Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.best: Travis Hunter, $1. He cost $16 in this room last September.
Miley 💨LEO 5K Speedo Fan Club.worst: Rashee Rice, $35. Up from $6, and there was no second bidder anywhere near that.

Good Will Hunting.headline: The best two players and then a cliff
body: Ja'Marr Chase at $63 and Christian McCaffrey at $59 is the strongest one-two punch anybody walked out with, and $122 of a $200 budget to own it. Seventy-two percent of his money sits in three players, the most concentrated roster in the league. When it works it looks like genius and when either man misses time it looks like the 2025 draft, where the five biggest buys finished sixth, fourteenth, 8-20, fourth and in the Sacco Bowl.

Then there is Jadarian Price at $22, a rookie running back who cost exactly the same as Jalen Hurts, Joe Burrow and Patrick Mahomes combined. That is the whole draft in one line. Terry McLaurin at $21 after going $30 last year is genuinely good work, and Joe Burrow at $11 is the third-best quarterback value of the night.

After McLaurin it is $5 and under for ten straight players. This is a lineup that wins six weeks by thirty and loses six weeks by thirty. In a fourteen-team league with six playoff spots, that is a coin flip dressed as a strategy.
Good Will Hunting.best: Terry McLaurin, $21. Nine dollars off last year's price for the same production.
Good Will Hunting.worst: Jadarian Price, $22. The same money as Hurts, Burrow and Mahomes put together.

ShakeNBake.headline: Three studs, two dollars, still no ring
body: Saquon Barkley $52, Ashton Jeanty $43, Nico Collins $43. A hundred and thirty-eight dollars, seventy percent of the budget, on three players, and all three came at a discount to last year's price in this room. That is the correct way to be top-heavy: buy the expensive guys when the market is soft rather than when it is peaking.

The trouble starts at pick four. Carnell Tate at $13 and Jonathon Brooks at $10 are dart throws being asked to hold down a flex, Mike Evans at $12 is the one piece of genuine middle-class value, and Trevor Lawrence at $7 is a quarterback bought on hope. Two dollars went unspent, which in an auction is two dollars set on fire.

Two runner-up finishes, no titles, fifteen seasons. The roster shape that produced both of those is exactly this one: an elite top, a soft middle, and a season that comes down to whether the third receiver hits. The man who built this website ranked himself seventh on it, which is the most honest thing on the page.
ShakeNBake.best: Mike Evans, $12. He cost $28 in this room a year ago.
ShakeNBake.worst: Carnell Tate, $13. A rookie asked to be the third receiver on a contender.

Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.headline: Sixty percent of the money on two names
body: Jaxon Smith-Njigba at $63 and James Cook III at $56. Those are the two biggest raises in the entire draft, plus $33 and plus $25 against what this room paid last September, and together they are $119 of a $200 budget. He did not find value on either one. He set the price on both and then had $81 left for fourteen more players.

What that $81 bought is a museum of other people's discounts: Alvin Kamara at $1 after $29, T.J. Hockenson at $1 after $8, Travis Kelce at $6 after $14, Keenan Allen at $1. Eight dollar players in total. Some of those hit. Enough of them will not.

And then there is Parker Washington at $21, which is more than he paid for DK Metcalf, more than three times what he paid for Travis Kelce, and the single most confident purchase anybody made all night on a player the rest of the room had priced at nothing. Bold. Genuinely bold. One playoff appearance in nine seasons says bold is overdue.
Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.best: Alvin Kamara, $1. Twenty-nine dollars last year, one dollar tonight.
Bend The Knee 🐲🔥.worst: Parker Washington, $21. Three and a half times what Travis Kelce cost him.

Mac Daddy.headline: Four receivers, one back, one boat
body: Jonathan Taylor at $62 is a $44 player from last year, so he paid eighteen dollars of tax to be certain, and then built a genuinely good receiver room behind him: DeVonta Smith $34, Tee Higgins $25, Garrett Wilson $23. Three starters plus a workhorse back is a playoff spine and he finished fourth last year with less.

The second running back is Rico Dowdle at $13, up from $2, and after that it is Kenny Gainwell at $6 and Tyler Allgeier at $2. In a lineup that starts two backs and two flexes, that is one injury away from a Tuesday morning waiver claim deciding the season.

George Kittle at $6 after $22 last year is the best tight end value in the draft. Lamar Jackson at $21 is the opposite: the second-most expensive quarterback in a league that pays four points for a passing touchdown, in a room where two quarterbacks went for $10 combined. That is not buying a player. That is buying a boat.
Mac Daddy.best: George Kittle, $6. Sixteen dollars cheaper than last year at a position nobody solved.
Mac Daddy.worst: Lamar Jackson, $21. Four-point passing touchdowns, one quarterback slot, twenty-one dollars.

Kim Jong Nate.headline: Two elite receivers and a backfield of strangers
body: CeeDee Lamb at $52 and Justin Jefferson at $51 is $103 on two wide receivers, and both came cheaper than last year, so the buys themselves are fine. Emeka Egbuka at $25 and Tyler Warren at $17 give him the best receiving corps in the league on paper. Then you look at the backfield.

The entire running back room cost $34. Quinshon Judkins at $23, Jacory Croskey-Merritt at $9, Kaleb Johnson at $1, Sean Tucker at $1. That is a starting lineup requirement of two backs plus two flexes being answered with one real player and three lottery tickets. A hundred and thirty-one dollars went to receivers and thirty-four went to the position that touches the ball on every snap.

Jayden Daniels at $10 after $21 last year is a clean win. Three dollars for a kicker in a scoring system that pays field goal yardage is fine. None of it changes the arithmetic: he bought two Ferraris and then had to get to work.
Kim Jong Nate.best: Jayden Daniels, $10. Half of last year's price for the same quarterback.
Kim Jong Nate.worst: The whole backfield, $34. Four running backs for less than one wide receiver cost him.

The Injured Reserved.headline: Sixteen players, two empty chairs
body: There is no kicker on this roster and no defense on this roster. Sixteen players, and two of the eleven starting slots cannot be filled. He will fix it on waivers Tuesday and it will cost him FAAB he should never have had to spend, and until then the lineup posts with holes in it. The team is called The Injured Reserved. It drafted itself onto injured reserve.

Which is a genuine shame, because the player-buying was excellent. Josh Jacobs at $8 is the single best purchase of the night, a $43 player in this room twelve months ago who came off the board fifth while fourteen people sat on their hands. Omarion Hampton $47, Zay Flowers $34 up from $17, Jaylen Waddle $24, Tucker Kraft $13, Chris Godwin $10. That is a deep, well-priced, playoff-quality roster.

It is also $28 on the bench, twice the league average, from a man who went 21-7 last year and finished fifth. The talent is top six. The roster construction is not, and in a league that mandates a kicker and a defense every week, the difference between those two things is a loss you can see coming in September.
The Injured Reserved.best: Josh Jacobs, $8. He cost $43 in this room last year and nobody bid.
The Injured Reserved.worst: No kicker and no defense. Two starting slots, zero players, sixteen roster spots used.

Leo the Cleo.headline: Seventy-three dollars on the first name called
body: Jahmyr Gibbs at $73 is the most expensive player in the fifteen-year history of this league. The old record was $70 for Ja'Marr Chase last season, and that team finished sixth. He nominated Gibbs first, bid against a room that was perfectly happy to let him have it, and spent thirty-seven percent of his budget before anybody else had bought a single player.

Then Josh Allen at $29, the most expensive quarterback in a draft where the entire quarterback market cost $153 across twenty-five players. Kyren Williams $32 and Malik Nabers $29 are both good buys. That is $163 in four men, and after Tony Pollard at $18 the roster falls off a table: nine players at $1 or $2, and a WR2 who cost four dollars.

Six seasons, zero playoff appearances, a 33-78 record and 4-24 last year. Aggression was the right instinct. Spending record money on one player and then filling nine roster spots out of the bargain bin is the same mistake this league makes every single September, and the receipts on it are printed one section down.
Leo the Cleo.best: Cooper Kupp, $2. He cost $11 here last year.
Leo the Cleo.worst: Jahmyr Gibbs, $73. The most expensive player in league history, bought before anybody else had spent a dollar.

FreeGucci.headline: He turned two hundred dollars into a smoothie
body: Sixteen players, exactly one of them cost a dollar, and not a single one cost more than $44. Chase Brown $44, George Pickens $37, DJ Moore $23, Drake Maye $15, Alec Pierce $14, Michael Pittman $13, Jordan Mason $13, Blake Corum $10. Every price in this draft is a mid-range price. There is no star to build around and no bargain to be glad about.

There is also no kicker and no individual defensive player, two mandatory starting slots left completely empty, and $5 of the budget never spent at all. $31 sits on the bench. Only $164 of his $200 is in a lineup that can actually be posted, second lowest in the league.

Three championships says he understands something the rest of us do not. This roster says whatever it is, it did not survive contact with a $37 bid on George Pickens, a $19 raise over last year for a receiver whose ceiling is somebody else's third option. Spreading money evenly is a strategy when the middle of the board is underpriced. Tonight it was not.
FreeGucci.best: Zach Charbonnet, $5. Six dollars off last year and a genuine handcuff.
FreeGucci.worst: Alec Pierce, $14. He cost a dollar in this room last September.

Hail Mary.headline: The title defense begins with three quarterbacks
body: The defending champion spent $22 on three quarterbacks in a league with one quarterback slot and four points for a passing touchdown. Jalen Hurts $8, Dak Prescott $8, Caleb Williams $6. He then spent $2 on two kickers for one kicker slot. He did not buy an individual defensive player at all, which is a mandatory position, so his Week 1 lineup has a hole in it before a single game kicks off.

Forty-eight dollars of his $200 is sitting on the bench, three and a half times the league average of $14, and his starting eleven cost $152, the lowest in the league by twenty dollars. His biggest single purchase all night was Jameson Williams at $28. Only thirty-eight percent of his budget is in his top three players, the flattest roster in the draft by a distance.

In 2025 he won this thing by refusing to buy anything expensive, and this site called his draft board the most boring document the league had ever produced. He appears to have read that as a compliment rather than a description of a market that happened to be soft. Flat is a strategy when the middle is cheap. This year the middle was the most expensive part of the board, and he is the commissioner, which means the man who wrote the roster rules is the only one in the league who did not fill them.
Hail Mary.best: TreVeyon Henderson, $13. Fifteen dollars off last year's price.
Hail Mary.worst: The second kicker. There is one kicker slot and no individual defensive player anywhere on the roster.
